content.thinking:
I'm planning the structure for a swamp troll model, roughly 2.6m tall and hunched, with chunky Warcraft-style proportions, tusks, mohawk, and bone fetishes, while being careful about coordinate axes and joint orientations to avoid type errors in the code.

Still working out limb lengths and joint chains...

Defining the spine chain and body loft stations next, starting with the pelvis region sized for the troll's characteristic big belly shape.

Finishing the loft with a final shoulder cap, then moving to coloring the troll's skin with mottled swamp green and a lighter countershaded belly, plus warts and subtle gradient paint. I'm also setting up the arm joints at the shoulders for the long reaching limbs.

Now I'm planning out the arm chain: positioning shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints at increasing outward angles so the troll's long arms hang down and to the side, parenting the chain to the spine, and tapering the arm sweep radius from shoulder to wrist before adding shoulder pad spheres.

I'm sketching the pauldron as a spiked bone-and-hide shoulder pad using a scaled sphere plus spikes, then working out simplified hands—palm boxes at the wrist with finger chains (four per hand, two joints each) to keep the rig manageable.

Setting up finger chains for each hand...

Now I'm setting up the neck chain with a couple curved spans leading into a small head joint with a heavy jaw, positioning it to jut forward from the last neck knot and parenting it appropriately to the spine.

Then I'm building the jaw joint and the head's facial geometry: a skull ellipsoid, brow ridge, glowing yellow eyes with pupils set under the brow, a flat wide nose with nostrils, and the beginnings of the muzzle sphere, all placed with explicit coordinates relative to the head bone.

Now I'm shaping the lower jaw with a pronounced underbite, adding curved tusk spikes swept upward from the jaw using bezier curves that rise past the upper lip, plus small upper fangs and rows of tooth spikes along the jawline before moving on to the ears.

I settle on a simple convex ear outline positioned on the skull with thin extrusion, then add gold torus earrings for detail. For the mohawk, I'm planning a row of extruded spiky plates following a curved path from forehead to crown to back of the neck, like a spine of flaming crimson fins.

Working through the spike direction and bone attachment logic for each plate along that path...

I'm reconsidering using extruded blade shapes instead of simple spikes for the mohawk, sketching outline points for each blade leaning backward in the sagittal plane.

I'll color each blade with a gradient from crimson at the base to orange at the tip, using a paint function that mixes the colors based on height. Then I'm placing the mohawk blades along the path, orienting each one's local axes relative to the curve direction.

For the shape of the mohawk itself, I'll split it into two paths—one tracing from forehead to nape along the skull, and a second continuing down the neck and spine, with blade size decreasing as it goes. I'll also plan a necklace of bone fetishes, skulls, and teeth strung around the neck.

For draping it onto the chest, I'm weighing between using the body's drape function with a rough collar-shaped loop near the shoulders versus building an explicit sweep path manually to avoid the surface-fitting wandering off unpredictably near the chest contours, accounting for how the spine's hunch shifts the chest depth at different heights.

Still working out necklace placement...

I realize I should pass the path frame itself as the base for the spike so it gets proper position and facing. For the bone fetishes, I'm thinking witch-doctor style decorations: skull trophies and feathered bone charms, placed on a neck necklace or belt rather than a staff, since the hand is already posed hanging down.

Now I'm working through where to position the belt loop around the hips joint — checking whether the cutting plane at that height actually wraps the torso surface correctly versus intersecting the leg tubes, since the belly is widest a bit higher up at y=1.35.

Now I'm placing the belt with a leather sweep, positioning the buckle at the front of the loop since t=0 aligns with world forward, and scattering hanging items near the start and end of the loop angles.

For the loincloth, I'm designing a front flap extruded as a ragged trapezoid hanging from the belt's front point, colored brown hide with paint stripe accents, positioned against the belly surface where the body's loft cross-section sits.

Still tuning loincloth geometry...

Now I'm designing the pauldrons as lathed dome shapes tilted outward at the shoulders, painted dark leather-brown, with a bony rim and a ring of spikes for extra detail.

Shoulder spikes auto-snap to the nearest joint, so that works fine without an explicit bone. For eyes, I'm planning small glowing spheres — green voodoo-flame style glow for the skull eyes to match the Blizzard-esque hand-painted aesthetic, using custom gradient paints instead of a toon shader kit.

I'm defining layered skin tones (light, mid, dark, belly) and combining mottle and countershade helpers to get a hand-painted reptilian highlight-and-shadow look with a lighter belly underside.

Then I'm scattering small wart bumps across the body mesh, planning around two dozen on the torso and fewer on the head, using a scatter filter so warts only land on the loft surface.

For texel density I figure a 2048 paint sheet gives decent resolution over roughly 12 square meters of surface, so I'll bump paintSize up in the builder config. Then for clothing, I'm sketching leather bracers as a sweep along the forearm with a slightly larger radius than the arm tube itself, cropped to a specific parameter range and reusing a radius function for consistency.

Now I'm planning brass rivet details stuck onto the bracer surface at a few angles around the tube, plus bone bead bands, before moving down to leg coverings -- loincloth, shin wraps, and bone anklets with a kneecap bump.

For the back, I'm adding a trapezius hump behind the neck and a row of bony spikes along the spine using the body loft's surface positions, keeping them oriented toward the dorsal side of the tube.

I'm also placing pec muscles as small spheres on the chest front, deriving their position by matching the loft's cross-section radius at that height, and considering whether the spine path should lean forward slightly to give the figure a hunched posture.

Checking the lean angle (around 17°) feels right for a hunched troll stance, with the head pitched forward. I'm also tracking the shoulder width, arm placement, and pauldron position relative to the neck path, but realize the total height with the mohawk is pushing close to 2.8m, which is taller than intended for this troll's proportions.

2.5-3m hunched height works fine for a swamp troll towering over a human, so I'll keep the head center around y=2.28. Now I'm placing the skull, brow ridge, and eye positions relative to the head joint, making sure the eyes sit below the heavy brow ridge with the skull thrust slightly forward.

For the muzzle and nose, I'm positioning a big bulbous troll nose with small dark nostril spheres protruding forward from the face.

Now I'm setting up the lower jaw: the chin, the dark flattened sphere for the mouth interior, and the small spike-cone teeth with tusks jutting from the lower jaw base.

For the tusks, I'm curving them up and outside the muzzle with three control points, keeping them clear of the nose width and tapering the tips down near the eyes so they don't look oversized, then adding a ring band detail around them.

Writing tusk gradient and bezier sweep code...

I'm considering small facial details like ears, chin, and skipping a beard, then thinking about adding tribal war paint using decal textures on the skull for forehead markings.

Writing decal SVG code...

For feet, I'm shaping a capsule sweep with a flat bottom to approximate a rounded box, adjusting the side radii to control width versus depth.

For toes, I'm adding three small capsules angled forward with claw-like spikes, mirrored symmetrically on each side of the ankle bone, plus a darker toenail cone for detail.

Now I'm checking the hip joint placement and leg segment lengths, working out root vectors and bend angles for the limb function so the leg chain connects properly from hip socket to ankle target.

For the leg chains, I'm setting up the hip-knee-ankle naming and parenting structure, then tuning the radius profile along the thigh to calf to ankle so the taper looks natural with a slight calf bulge.

Now I'm adding a knee cap sphere positioned slightly forward of the knee joint for a bit of anatomical bulge, then moving on to the arm chain—placing shoulder, elbow, and wrist positions so the arms hang angled outward and slightly forward with a hunched, thick look.

I'm tapering the arm radii from shoulder to wrist and naming the joint chain for shoulder/elbow/wrist parented to the spine, then working out palm box placement centered off the wrist position for the hands.

Still shaping the palm geometry...

Now I'm working out the finger chains, computing symmetric base x-offsets along the palm bottom and sketching each finger's joint path with a forward curl from knuckle to tip.

Working out claw spikes using the chain's base frame and bone direction, then sketching the thumb's path coordinates with inward-facing x offsets scaled from the hand size.

I shift the thumb slightly outward to avoid collision with the first finger, keeping the palm half-width reasonable so the thumb sits just outside it. I need to grab the wrist tip from the arm's last joint since the chain's typed `tip` property isn't reliable, then plan the pauldron geometry — a lathed dome, bone rim torus, and a ring of spikes — mirrored with slight variance for each shoulder.

I'm now sketching hanging feather fetishes off the pauldron rim using small card planes with a feather SVG texture (teal body, red accents, gradient fill), positioned so they dangle outward without clipping into the arm as it swings down and out from the shoulder.

Beyond the feathers, I'm planning a bone totem for the back — crossed femur-like bones strapped with a skull bundle, placed just above the chest's back hump so it sits naturally between the shoulders.

Adding bone geometry and shoulder straps...

Closing the sash loop around the torso with a full set of draped points, then adding bone beads, a skull pendant, and fang trophies hung along the front portion of the sash using a partial sweep range.

I'm checking that the closed-path draping carries over knots correctly, then considering a separate neck choker made of bone beads as a ring around the neck rather than duplicating the sash as a necklace.

Writing bead and cord placement code...

Working out that angle 0 is up-and-back while 180 is front, so for an even item count the pendant naturally lands at the front position. I'm planning a separate skull helper that builds a cranium sphere, jaw box, and eye sockets, then placing it hanging below the front neck item using that item's position.

Designing the skull geometry: a cranium sphere with a slightly flattened shape, a jawbone box below it, a small teeth strip, dark eye socket spheres, and a nose hole, with optional glowing inner spheres nested in the sockets for a subtle eerie effect.

I'm budgeting around seven skulls across the belt, buckle, and dangles so the total part count stays manageable, planning them to face forward by default along the belt loop. Now I'm sketching a fetish-bundle helper that wraps crossed bones with cord and feathers for extra ornamentation.

Still writing geometry logic...

Working out the rotation direction so t=0.25 lands on +X and t=0.75 on -X, then placing skulls, fetishes, and dangles at specific t values around the belt loop with the back flap at t=0.5. For bone attachment I'm leaning toward the hips joint since the loop sits at hip level, though spine1 might work better.

I'm confirming the body loft spans the right vertical range to catch the belt plane, then writing a helper function to pull x/y/z coordinates off the Vector3 points returned by the path's `.at(t)` so the hanging belt items can be positioned correctly.

I'm then planning scatter wart placements on the skin surface using a filter and seeded RNG, and sketching out a chest decal idea—maybe a tribal spiral war-paint design in teal and white.

For hair details, I'm adding a lighter brow capsule and glowing yellow eyes with small black pupils, plus chin braids with bone beads sweeping down like a troll beard.

Mohawk gets a hot orange-red color with yellow tips for contrast against green skin, braids in a darker crimson tone, keeping the overall palette capped at 64 flat colors.

I'm defining mottled textures for leather and hide pieces—loincloth, belt—using subtle patch and mottle patterns with small seeds and sizes to keep things grounded and painterly without needing extra geometry.

For the bones I'll keep flat colors but add gradients to the larger ones, and skin stays consistent across sweeps, parts, and lofts since the paint function reads position and normal data regardless of geometry type.

Now I'm working out teeth placement—upper fangs as spike pairs and a lower row of small bone spikes positioned along a curved jawline using a simple index-based loop for x and z offsets.

I'm checking that the tusk roots and tooth bases sit correctly relative to the chin sphere's geometry so they appear anchored rather than floating, working through the radius math to confirm the base points fall just inside or on the chin's surface.

Now I'm tracing whether the upper and lower jaw spheres overlap properly to form a closed mouth versus a snarl gap — the chin sphere's top and the muzzle sphere's bottom need to meet without leaving an ugly visible dark gap, so I'm adjusting their y-centers (chin down to 2.1, muzzle up to 2.26) to get a believable closed bite with just enough overlap.

I decide to skip rendering the mouth interior cavity since it's mostly hidden at this scale, and simplify the teeth to just the tusks plus a lower row rather than adding upper teeth spikes that would just overlap messily. I'm leaning toward a neutral rest pose with the mouth slightly open rather than fully shut.

Adding the mouth cavity sphere and pink tongue on the jaw, confirming the rotation axis opens the jaw downward correctly. I should also add a gold nose ring as a small torus near the nose.

Now I'm working out ear earrings and verifying the ear geometry mirrors correctly left to right using the sign variable for outward positioning.

For the long pointy troll ears, I want tips swept back rather than straight out, so I'm adjusting the direction vector to angle outward and backward, which should keep the thickness calculation valid. Skipping any ear tuft detail, and now moving on to checking whether hands should have bracers.

Now I'm adding ankle bands with small teeth-like spikes ringing the leg joint, plus a leather band sweep layered over the tapered leg radius, matching similar bracer treatment at the wrists with rivets. I'm also planning spikes running along the spine using a loft-based placement function to space them evenly down the back.

Checking the orientation logic, the spikes on a nearly-vertical tube should point outward from the dorsal side since that's the "back" normal relative to world-up, so I'll color them a dark horn tone with ridge detailing. I'm also adding a hunched trapezius hump near the shoulders for silhouette, then laying out a crossed-bone rack behind the back, working out rod endpoints that intersect near the upper spine.

Working through surface offsets at several heights, I'm nudging the rod endpoints outward by about 0.05 so they visually rest on the surface rather than sink into it, then placing a skull piece at the crossing point oriented to face the body.

Since my skull helper defaults to facing +z but this one needs to face -z, I'm adding a sign parameter that flips the z offsets for orientation. I'm attaching the back bones to the spine joint, and planning out the full joint hierarchy -- hips, spine segments, neck, head, jaw, arm chains with finger joints, and leg chains with their endpoint joints.

Working through the spine and neck chains now, deciding how catmull-rom knot spans map to joint counts and names, and confirming parent references so the head attaches correctly to the neck chain and the neck attaches to the spine. I'm also checking that the loft and sweep calls accept joint, chain, or list references for bones, and verifying the skull and neck radii line up smoothly at the join point before placing the brow capsule.

Now I'm positioning facial features: calculating the brow's z-offset from the skull's curvature so it sits slightly proud of the surface, then placing eye sockets, eyeballs, and pupils with small z-offsets to make them protrude correctly and glow appropriately. I'm also adding cheekbone spheres and double-checking forehead placement before considering whether to add hair or a mohawk shape at the back of the head.

Still working out mohawk curve points...

Still computing spine positions...

Writing blade height function...

Still writing extrusion code...

For the feather, I'm sketching an SVG shape with a teal leaf-like outline, darker center stripe, red side barbs, and a small eye-spot detail near the top, sized to fit the pauldron proportions.

Now I'm designing war paint SVGs for the chest and cheeks using white and red diagonal slashes, plus a separate teal spiral tattoo motif built from an arc path.

For placement, I'm deciding whether the decal needs to target multiple body parts or if I should simplify by dropping the pec spheres so the chest loft surface stays clean enough to display the spiral decal clearly.

Now I'm sketching out the imports and helper modules I'll need: builder types, skeleton joints, frame utilities, RNG, path curves, IK limb helpers, and the various shading/paint utilities like gradients, mottling, stripes, and patches for coloring the mesh.

Writing color paint definitions...

Writing moss patch logic...

Now I'm defining more materials: leather with patches, a dark belt mottle, bone colors for flat and detailed tones, and spikes for the pauldron using bone. Then I start building the main function, setting up the builder with the troll's name and paint size before constructing the skin.

Writing joint hierarchy...

Building each leg chain from hip through knee to ankle, mirrored left and right, with contact points for ground placement.

Confirming the ankle joint is the third tip joint, then building the foot sweep with a straight two-point path and radius function returning a tuple, working through the TypeScript typing so the array literal satisfies the readonly pair type.

Writing toe sweeps and claw spikes...

For the leg wraps, I'm working out an approximate radius function interpolating between key thickness values along the shin, since there's no interpolation helper available—just hand-computing the taper at the relevant t positions.

Now I'm sweeping the leather wrap along the leg using that radius formula, then adding an ankle band and a ring of small bone spikes around the leg at t=0.94 to form teeth-like decoration.

Moving to the arms, I'm setting up shoulder, elbow, and wrist points to build a chain with a polyline through those three joints, creating a swept tube that smooths the corners at the elbow for a rounded limb shape.

Still tuning bracer radius profile... adding brass rivet studs around the bracer at a couple of positions ensure that proud offset from the arm tube stays consistent along its length.

I'm adding bone elbow spikes projecting outward from the joint, then shaping pauldron shoulder armor as a tilted lathe dome positioned above where the arms begin.

Now I'm adding a bone torus ring at the pauldron's base, oriented along the normalized shoulder axis, then setting up spikes standing outward from that ring with a tilt toward the upward direction.

I'm placing six spikes in a ring embedded partially into the dome so they emerge with an outward-upward tilt, adding a single larger top spike, then starting to position three hanging feather frames near the base.

Skipping the shoulder skull idea, keeping the top spike as is. For hands, I'm parenting fingers to the wrist joint at the tip of the arm chain, giving each finger a tapering radius and considering small knuckle spheres at the base positions. I'm also sorting out which parts belong to the head bone versus the jaw.

Adding a tongue sphere inside the jaw, then working out a bone-like circlet band wrapping around the forehead beneath the mohawk, computing the ellipse geometry for the ring path using the skull's radius at that height.

Adding bone bead studs along the band and a few decorative spikes across the front arc, keeping part counts in check, then starting on a sash drape built from the body surface.

Placing teeth spikes along the drape path near the sash front, and checking the catmull curve closes properly through the seven drape points. I'll add bead rings threaded along the sash as well, skipping extra stitching details like buttons.

Now I'm writing a boneRod helper that draws a rod between two points with sphere joints at each end, keyed to a bone for skeletal attachment.

Writing skull helper...

Still building the skull geometry...

Placing belt attachments next: a skull buckle positioned on the belt curve, small skull and spike decorations scattered along the belt at specific parameter points, plus the loincloth's front and back flaps hanging from the belt midpoint and center-back.

I'm defining the ragged outline for the loincloth flap as a closed polygon with sharp points for its jagged bottom edge, then extruding it along the belt with a tilted y-axis so it drapes forward and down.

For the back piece I'm mirroring the x-axis, setting a thin leather thickness, and considering extra details like bone trim or a decal but deciding to keep the leather patches plain. I'm also sketching out a small hip pouch as a leather box with a flap and cord, positioned under the belt on one side.

Now I'm working out the offset for that pouch placement, settling on a rough approximation rather than exact trig, then moving on to finalize the color palette—bone, claw, brass, eye glow, pupil, and tongue tones.

With colors locked, I'm assigning flat paint for warts and hair accents, checking the mohawk height brings total troll height to around 2.8m which feels acceptable for a hunched 2.5m creature. I'm also considering adding war paint decals to the skull via a decal API, deciding to keep them but maybe restrict to the cheek, and planning a simple SVG slash texture for the war paint.

Writing SVG decal code...

Still assembling the model...

Setting up the belt loop and checking frame arguments, then sketching the leg import path and finger-chain naming for nested loops. I'm also considering adding moss or grass card tufts scattered across the shoulders and back for a swampy texture.

Still writing the moss texture SVG and pauldron vector/lathe setup...

Still building the creature...

Shaping the angry brow slope and tusk paths per side, then finalizing the root pose and adding moss tuft textures before writing the file.
